analysis.title: US Rates Watch: Monthly rates models: Nov '26 edition
key_insights: BofA's macro model puts 10-year Treasury fair value at about 4.5-4.7%, up roughly 0-5bp over the past month with a wider range (more uncertainty). Treasuries trade more than 2 standard deviations cheap to macro fundamentals but have partly recoupled with macro data over the past month.
The 10-year Treasury yield fair value consistent with global yields is about 5.15%, down about 10bp over the month. The 10-year trades fair to that framework (residual +0.8bp, 0.0 sigma).

BofA says a material 10-year selloff would need either broader bearish momentum in global yields or a decoupling of US growth from developed-market growth (a return to American exceptionalism). In late cycle, Treasuries should trade fair to rich versus global yields.
Macro factor momentum is mixed over the past month: Broad Macro +0.17 sigma, Growth -0.12, Inflation -0.14, Employment -0.14. The reflation theme persists but data dispersion is wider.

Only about 45% of the 10-year yield move over the past 3 months is explained by macro data. 10-year yields rose about 6bp over 1 month, 14bp over 2 months and 40bp over 3 months, against fair value changes of about -2bp, -1bp and +18bp.

On the DFM macro framework, Treasuries are cheap across the curve: 2y +2.34 sigma, 5y +2.47, 10y +2.12, 30y +1.92. BofA notes a 2 sigma 10-year residual historically mean reverts over 3-6 months, but it expects the reversion to be backloaded into end 2027.

Front-end moves are driving about 85% of 2s10s curve dynamics over the past 2 weeks, versus 57-80% over the prior 1-2 months. Bull steepening (42%) and bear flattening (43%) were about equally frequent over 2 weeks. Dispersion is about 85% versus a historical average of about 70%, which BofA reads as low but rising macro conviction.
In 5s30s, the belly drove about 94% of moves over the past 2 weeks. Bear flattening still dominates (54% over 2 weeks) although momentum has faded.

BofA expects the SOFR/FF basis to print wider in mid 2027, driven by debt limit dynamics. It forecasts the debt limit to bind in Feb 2027 and be resolved in Aug 2027, with funding conditions softening and downward pressure on SOFR in between. The model implies a wider basis than market pricing for mid 2027, consistent with BofA's view to be long SOFR/FF futures.

Funding conditions tightened temporarily in October but stayed benign despite a slow liquidity drain. BofA attributes this to lower demand for funding (less hedge fund leverage, money market funds staying short on Fed path uncertainty) outweighing lower supply.
10-year breakevens trade about 20-25bp tight to fair value (about 245-255bp). 10-year real yields trade about 75-80bp cheap to fair value of about 2.1%.

Breakevens imply only about 20-25% likelihood of an expansion scenario, down from about 85% in early October. Slowdown is the dominant signal, and credit markets (EM credit, IG CDX, HY CDX) show equal or lower expansion likelihoods than breakevens.

Risk sentiment deteriorated over the past month. Futures positioning bias fell to about 35% from about 53% in early October. ETF flows show short bias in US small and large cap equities, material short bias in high yield, short bias in gold and energy, and a marginal long bias in equity vol.

The equity risk premium widened about 25bp over the month but remains historically tight (more than 1 sigma). BofA says this creates scope for negative feedback loops between bond selloffs and risk assets, which could close into a Treasury bid if selloffs are not accompanied by earnings upgrades.

Tail scenario likelihoods rose to about 40-45%: recession about 20-25% and reflation about 15-20%. Market-implied scenario likelihoods are hard landing 20-25%, soft landing 40-50%, no landing 10-20%, reacceleration/reflation 15-20%.

Global 10-year relative value: France is 4.2 sigma cheap (from 4.4 in early Oct), Japan 1.7 sigma cheap (from 2.5), Belgium 1.1 sigma cheap. Austria, Holland and Germany are rich. The US is at fair value (0.0 sigma).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Model fair value consistent with current US fundamentals. The 10-year at about 5.14% trades more than 2 sigma cheap to it.
Down about 10bp over the month. The 10-year trades fair to global yields.
Market breakevens trade about 20-25bp tight to fair value.
Real yields trade about 75-80bp cheap to fair value.
Model implies a wider SOFR/FF basis than futures price for mid 2027 because of debt limit dynamics.
Funding conditions soften and SOFR faces downward pressure while the limit binds.
Effective fed funds has been sticky around 2bp below IORB for several months.

trade_ideas.description: Long SOFR/FF futures (wider SOFR/FF basis in mid 2027)
trade_ideas.rationale: BofA's model implies a wider SOFR/FF basis than current market pricing for mid 2027 because the debt limit softens funding conditions and pressures SOFR lower.

risk_factors: Tail risks on the curve have risen: recession about 20-25% and reflation about 15-20%, together about 40-45%.
Front-end (Fed) driven curve moves dominate, so Fed path uncertainty is the main driver of rates volatility.
Tight equity risk premium creates scope for negative feedback loops between bond yield selloffs and risk assets.
Long equity vol bias and a risk-off shift in positioning and flows make carry trades challenging in US and EM credit.
Debt limit dynamics in 2027 could shift funding conditions and the SOFR/FF basis.
BofA's macro models tend to break down when there is large non-economic buying of Treasuries.

tension_points.bull_case: Treasuries trade more than 2 sigma cheap to macro fair value (about 4.5-4.7% vs 5.14% actual), and a 2 sigma residual has historically mean reverted over 3-6 months, which implies lower yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Reversion is expected to be backloaded into end 2027. Macro explains only about 45% of the 3-month yield rise, and the 10-year trades fair to global yields at about 5.15%, so cheapness may persist.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A material 10yT selloff would need broader bearish momentum in global yields or a decoupling of US growth from the developed-market complex (American exceptionalism).

tension_points.theme: equity risk premium and bond selloffs
tension_points.bull_case: Further bond selloffs not accompanied by earnings upgrades could close into a bid for Treasuries as risk assets weaken.
tension_points.bear_case: Tight ERP (more than 1 sigma) creates scope for negative feedback loops between bond yield selloffs and risky assets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bond selloffs accompanied by upgrades to earnings would break the feedback loop.
